title: Three-level CodeGraph context retrieval
refined_problem: The harness currently selects bounded repository files with a lightweight dependency graph, but agents still receive more file content than necessary and symbol-level retrieval is absent. This increases context cost and makes it harder to pass precise, reproducible context to each AI provider.

original_request.text: Bueno creame todo lo que se tenga que ver para este modelo, sprint epic, task etcm para empezar una nueva conversacion y empezar con esto
original_request.canonical_english: Create all durable planning artifacts needed for the three-level CodeGraph and context-retrieval initiative, including its epic, features, executable tasks, and sprint, so implementation can begin in a new conversation.

translation.back_translation: Crear todos los artefactos durables de planificación necesarios para la iniciativa de CodeGraph y recuperación de contexto de tres niveles, incluyendo su épica, funcionalidades, tareas ejecutables y sprint, para que la implementación pueda comenzar en una nueva conversación.

target_users: Harness coordinators preparing context for implementation, review, verification, and audit agents
AI agents that need a minimal reproducible repository context pack
Repository maintainers who need auditable reasons for context inclusion and token usage
outcomes: Agents receive a minimal, reproducible context pack rather than broad repository content.
Repository, file, and symbol retrieval remain provider-neutral and work with the existing harness lifecycle.
Every selected node, file, symbol, or snippet has an auditable inclusion reason, size, token estimate, and hash.
The system measures context reduction without silently sacrificing relevant implementation or test coverage.
success_metrics: A representative task produces deterministic repository, file, and symbol retrieval results across repeated runs.
The context pack remains within configured file, byte, and token budgets.
The benchmark reports token reduction and relevant-surface recall against the current file-level compiler.
Secret and generated-path exclusions remain enforced in every retrieval level.
The existing test suite remains green and provider activation continues to consume the context pack.

in: Update codegraph.md into the durable implementation specification.
Define a normalized repository graph with an optional CodeGraph backend and the current local graph as fallback.
Extend context_compiler.py for graph-aware file retrieval and auditable budgeted output.
Add symbol indexing and bounded snippet extraction, starting with Python and using safe fallback behavior for unsupported languages.
Add schemas, tests, and a deterministic token-savings benchmark.
out: A mandatory external CodeGraph service or dependency.
Embeddings, vector databases, or semantic search infrastructure.
Replacing the Harness ACI or changing provider-specific model selection.
A perfect semantic call graph for every supported programming language.
Sending full exploration transcripts to the main agent.

mvp.goal: Deliver an end-to-end, provider-neutral context pipeline that retrieves a bounded repository graph, relevant files, and Python symbols/snippets while preserving the existing fallback behavior.
includes: Local normalized graph backend with optional backend selection.
File ranking and context budget accounting.
Python class/function/method ranges and bounded snippets.
Fallback to complete files when symbol extraction is unavailable or unsafe.
Deterministic tests and a baseline-versus-snippet token benchmark.
excludes: JavaScript/TypeScript AST extraction beyond a safe follow-up slice.
Automatic changes to agent prompts or provider adapters unless required by the context-pack contract.

business_rules: Explicit task files and policy-mandated files are never dropped solely because a symbol extractor cannot process them.
A context result must be reproducible from task input, policy, repository state, and the selected graph backend.
Unsupported or malformed source must degrade to a bounded safe fallback rather than producing misleading snippets.
The external CodeGraph backend is optional; the local graph remains the availability fallback.
Token savings cannot justify leaking excluded paths or removing acceptance-critical tests.
data_and_integrations: Repository source files and task metadata are the authoritative inputs.
harness/context-policy.json owns limits, exclusions, backend selection, and retrieval behavior.
The optional CodeGraph integration must be local or explicitly configured and must not contact external services during ordinary task activation.
context.json and context-graph.json remain durable run artifacts under .harness/runs/<task-id>/.
security_privacy: Reuse the existing exclusion policy for secrets, VCS internals, generated output, and oversized files.
Do not transmit source content to an external graph service by default.
Hash and audit selected content without storing credentials or secret-like values in planning or context artifacts.
operational_constraints: The implementation must run on the repository's supported Windows environment and remain provider-neutral.
The existing context compiler must continue to work when CodeGraph is unavailable.
The output must respect configured max_files, max_total_bytes, and max_total_tokens_estimate limits.
The first implementation should avoid adding a dependency unless a concrete backend contract requires it.
assumptions: CodeGraph is treated as a backend capability behind a normalized repository-graph contract, not as a mandatory named vendor product.
Python is the first language with structural symbol extraction because the repository's control plane is primarily Python.
Current lexical import resolution and test affinity are a valid fallback baseline.
A 10-unit first sprint is preferable to filling the default 12-unit capacity with unvalidated polish.

open_questions.question: Which concrete external CodeGraph implementation, if any, should be connected after the local contract is proven?
open_questions.resolution: Defer provider selection; implement the adapter contract and local fallback first.

open_questions.question: What minimum token-reduction target should become a release gate after benchmark data exists?
open_questions.resolution: Measure baseline and candidate first; set the target from observed recall/cost trade-offs.

challenges: Regex-only imports do not provide complete semantic dependency or call information.
Overly aggressive snippet trimming can omit decorators, imports, class context, or tests.
Different languages require different symbol extraction strategies.
A broad graph can increase retrieval cost if graph expansion is not bounded and scored.
The context artifact must remain auditable and compatible with current provider activation.

work_items.title: Three-level CodeGraph context retrieval
work_items.description: Provide a provider-neutral retrieval capability that narrows repository context from graph, to files, to symbols and snippets while preserving deterministic evidence and safe fallbacks.
outcomes: Safe fallback when graph or symbol extraction is unavailable

work_items.title: Normalized repository graph
work_items.description: Expose repository modules, packages, files, tests, and bounded dependency relationships through an optional CodeGraph backend with the current local graph as fallback.

work_items.title: Budgeted file context retrieval
work_items.description: Use the normalized graph and task metadata to select relevant files with deterministic ranking, explicit inclusion reasons, hashes, and token budgets.

work_items.title: Symbol and snippet retrieval
work_items.description: Select the classes, functions, methods, and bounded source regions needed by a task, starting with Python and falling back safely to complete files.

work_items.title: Context efficiency measurement
work_items.description: Compare current file-level context with graph-and-symbol retrieval and report token reduction, relevant-surface recall, determinism, and fallback usage.

tasks.title: Define normalized graph contract and local fallback
tasks.description: Define and implement a normalized repository-graph contract with an optional CodeGraph backend, the existing lexical graph as a deterministic fallback, bounded graph expansion, policy-based exclusions, and durable graph metadata.
acceptance_criteria: The graph output has a versioned normalized shape for nodes, edges, backend identity, repository paths, and deterministic counts.
The configured auto backend uses CodeGraph only when available and otherwise uses the local graph without failing task activation.
Graph construction respects context-policy exclusions and bounded source-size limits.
Repeated graph construction over the same repository and policy produces stable node and edge ordering.
Tests cover imports, reverse references, test affinity, cycles, missing imports, exclusions, backend unavailability, and malformed source fallback.

tasks.title: Extend context compiler with graph-aware file retrieval
tasks.description: Extend the context compiler to consume the normalized graph, rank task-relevant files, preserve explicit and policy-required files, enforce context budgets, and emit auditable file-level context metadata.
acceptance_criteria: The compiler uses explicit files, policy-required files, task terms, memory, graph neighbors, and related tests as bounded ranking inputs.
Every selected file records path, bytes, estimated tokens, sha256, score, and inclusion reasons.
The compiler never exceeds configured file, byte, or token limits except for explicitly required files according to current policy semantics.
The output remains backward-compatible with current context.json consumers and identifies the graph backend used.
Tests cover ranking determinism, budget boundaries, explicit-file precedence, graph neighbors, memory, tests, and secret/generated-path exclusions.

tasks.title: Add Python symbol and snippet retrieval
tasks.description: Add structural Python symbol indexing and bounded snippet extraction to the context pipeline, selecting relevant classes, functions, and methods while retaining safe complete-file fallback for unsupported or unsafe extraction.
acceptance_criteria: The symbol index reports classes, functions, and methods with stable names and exact source line ranges.
Snippet selection uses task terms, graph relationships, explicit references, and related tests without exceeding the context budget.
Selected snippets record path, symbol, start_line, end_line, hash, token estimate, and inclusion reason.
Imports, decorators, class context, and required surrounding syntax are preserved or the compiler falls back to the complete file.
Tests cover nested symbols, malformed Python, empty matches, deterministic ordering, line boundaries, budget limits, and fallback behavior.

tasks.title: Measure context savings and relevant-surface recall
tasks.description: Create a deterministic benchmark that compares current file-level retrieval with graph-and-symbol retrieval, reports token savings and relevant-surface recall, and documents safe rollout criteria.
acceptance_criteria: The benchmark runs against fixed repository task fixtures without contacting external services.
The report includes baseline tokens, candidate tokens, reduction percentage, selected files, selected symbols, fallback count, and relevant-surface recall.
The benchmark detects regressions where token reduction comes from omitting explicit files, required tests, or policy-mandated context.
The rollout recommendation keeps the existing file-level behavior as the safe default until benchmark evidence supports enabling snippets.
The benchmark output and documentation explain how future repositories can reproduce the measurement.

proposed_sprint.goal: Deliver the first end-to-end provider-neutral context pipeline from normalized repository graph to budgeted files and Python symbols, with deterministic evidence and measured token savings.

execution_waves.exit_condition: Normalized graph contract, fallback, policy boundaries, and tests pass.
File-level context output remains compatible and budgeted with durable reasons and hashes.
Python symbol/snippet retrieval works with safe fallback and deterministic tests.
Token savings and relevant-surface recall are measured and documented.

proposed_sprint.selection_rationale: This order creates a vertical slice while resolving graph-contract uncertainty before compiler and symbol work. It uses 10 of 12 capacity units and leaves slack for integration findings.

research_rdd.rationale: The MVP uses repository-answerable local evidence and a reversible provider-neutral adapter boundary; no external contract is selected yet.
